task_summary: The agent had to produce a modified workbook that fills F2:H20 with rows from the source spreadsheet sorted by the helper list in J, preserving source order within each helper group, skipping blanks/headers/duplicate NAME+REF pairs, and falling back to A-Z only if J is empty.

explicit: Write the modified spreadsheet to `/app/output/1_22-47_output.xlsx` using Python.
Fill only `F2:H20` according to the helper-column sort rules, duplicate skipping rules, and the alphabetical fallback when column J is empty.
implicit: The verifier compares exact cell values in `F2:H20`, so the ITEM column in the output must be renumbered sequentially rather than copied from source ITEM values.
Repeated header blocks and duplicate `NAME+REF` rows in the source workbook must be filtered before writing the answer range.
missed_implicit: The verifier compares exact cell values in `F2:H20`, so the ITEM column in the output must be renumbered sequentially rather than copied from source ITEM values.
instructions.evidence: Step 10: "Created Python solution at `/app/solve_spreadsheet.py:1` ... Filled only the requested output range `F2:H20` ... Used helper list in column `J` first, preserving source order within each matched name group ..."; test stdout: "Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at F2: gt=1, proc=5".

closeness_to_success.explanation: The agent got the helper-priority ordering and duplicate handling right, but the first output cell was wrong because it carried over the source ITEM value instead of starting the output numbering at 1. The verifier failed immediately on `F2` with `gt=1, proc=5`.

superficial_cause.summary: The output workbook kept the source ITEM number in the first sorted row instead of writing the expected sequential output index.
superficial_cause.evidence_quote: test_stdout.txt:887:  Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at F2: gt=1, proc=5

root_cause.summary: The agent modeled the task as copying sorted source rows into F:H, but the answer range expects a freshly constructed list whose ITEM values are regenerated after filtering and sorting. That mismatch is visible in the final failure at F2.
root_cause.evidence_quote: Step 10: "Used helper list in column `J` first, preserving source order within each matched name group"; test_stdout.txt:887: `Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at F2: gt=1, proc=5`

failing_test_evidence.what_verifier_checks: tests/evaluate.py:174-188 loads the processed and answer workbooks and compares each cell in the parsed `answer_position`; `tests/evaluate.py:204-224` loops over the single test case and prints PASS/FAIL on the first mismatched cell. `tests/config.json:2-6` sets `id` to `22-47`, `answer_position` to `F2:H20`, and `num_test_cases` to `1`.
failing_test_evidence.what_agent_produced: Step 10 says the agent created `/app/solve_spreadsheet.py:1`, generated `/app/output/1_22-47_output.xlsx`, and filled `F2:H20`, but the verifier observed `proc=5` at `F2` instead of the expected `1`.
failing_test_evidence.exact_failure_quote: Test case 1: FAIL — Value diff at F2: gt=1, proc=5

super_capable_counterfactual.claim: If the agent had renumbered the sorted output rows starting from 1 instead of copying the source ITEM values, the trial would have passed.
super_capable_counterfactual.X: Rewrite the first column of `F2:H20` as sequential output indices after filtering and sorting, while keeping the NAME and REF columns unchanged.
super_capable_counterfactual.Y: Keep the source ITEM values attached to the sorted rows when writing the output range.

issues: The benchmark package ships fixed answer files under `tests/answer_files`, and the canonical oracle solution copies them into `/app/output`; if those paths are exposed to the agent runtime, the task becomes trivially bypassable.
task_quality.structural_hackability_notes: The verifier reads `/tests/answer_files/*.xlsx` and compares against the output workbook cell-by-cell. The canonical oracle solution in `solution/solve.sh` simply copies the answer workbook, so any runtime exposure of those paths would let an agent bypass the intended spreadsheet transformation.

notes_for_aggregation: This is a near-miss rather than a bad sort: the helper-order logic matched the answer workbook, and the first observable divergence was the ITEM renumbering at F2. Aggregators should bucket this as a mostly-correct spreadsheet transformation with an output-indexing bug.
